answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: The saying is credited to Beauvoir in a quotation compilation cited by Wikiquote: The Book of Positive Quotations (2007), page 525. No original French passage, English translator, or primary Beauvoir publication has been established here.

author.name: Simone de Beauvoir
author.heading: About Simone de Beauvoir
author.bio: Simone de Beauvoir wrote philosophical essays, fiction and memoir, placing human freedom within concrete social circumstances. The Second Sex became a foundational feminist work, while her wartime and postwar writing repeatedly examined the effects of one person’s choices on others.

cite.sourceCitation: Cook, John, compiler; Steve Deger and Leslie Ann Gibson, editors. The Book of Positive Quotations. Fairview Press, 2007, 525, as cited by Wikiquote. Original Beauvoir source and translator unestablished.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘Defending the truth is not something one does out of a sense of duty or to allay guilt complexes, but is a reward in itself’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

copyAttribution: Attributed to Simone de Beauvoir in The Book of Positive Quotations (2007), p. 525, as cited by Wikiquote; original work and English translator unconfirmed.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The saying presents truthful advocacy as valuable in itself, rather than a performance motivated by obligation or guilt. That is an interpretation of the circulating words, not proof that they belong to a particular Beauvoir argument.

Beauvoir’s ethics does examine freedom and responsibility within social life, but thematic compatibility cannot authenticate a quotation. Until an original work and translation are located, the specific compilation citation should travel with the attribution’s limit.
